- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent high.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73.0), model often overshoots → cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +1.0–1.5% below peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.4) and price is trending down, model underreacts → add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast days are above 72.0, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until price stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward momentum in negative sentiment periods → add 0.2–0.6% downward bias to forecast if sentiment avg < -0.2 over last 7 days.
